Do not give me a collaboration story. Draft the one-page architecture decision record: context, options, decision criteria, chosen topology, rejected alternatives, measurable risks, experiment, and reversal condition. I will challenge any criterion that cannot be observed.
turns.expected_stems: draft architecture decision record context options criteria chosen topology rejected alternatives measurable|principal engineer wants swarm customer routing because flexible compliance deterministic workflow auditable

turns.text: You are mentoring an engineer whose pull request adds an agent with free-form outputs, no deadline, broad account tools, and logs containing raw prompts. Produce five concrete review comments, each tied to a failure mode, and rewrite the acceptance criteria for the pull request. Then show the smallest test you would pair-program first rather than taking the implementation away from the engineer.
turns.expected_stems: produce concrete review comments failure rewrite acceptance criteria request smallest would program|mentoring engineer whose request agent outputs deadline broad account tools containing prompts

turns.text: An AI support assistant has told customers that pending withdrawals were complete. Produce the first fifteen minutes of the incident command log: timestamped actions, named roles, containment, evidence preservation, customer-impact query, decision owner, and internal communication. Include the exact condition for disabling only the unsafe answer path while preserving read-only case lookup.
turns.expected_stems: produce first fifteen minutes incident command timestamped actions named roles containment evidence|support assistant customers pending withdrawals complete produce first fifteen minutes incident command

turns.text: A compliance officer asks, "Why did the agent tell this customer that tax was withheld?" Draw a decision-lineage artifact from authenticated request through tools, source records, policy version, model invocation, output checks, and human handoff. Then give a two-paragraph explanation suitable for Compliance that distinguishes verified facts, deterministic policy, model-generated wording, and unresolved uncertainty.
turns.expected_stems: compliance officer agent customer withheld decision lineage artifact authenticated request through tools|compliance officer agent customer withheld decision lineage artifact authenticated request through tools

turns.text: Live coding: write validate_agent_manifest in Python. The manifest must declare owner, purpose, allowed_data_classes, tool capabilities, max_steps, timeout_seconds, evaluation_suite, rollback_action, and human_escalation. Return every violation in stable sorted order; do not stop at the first error. Add tests for a valid manifest and one with a write-capable tool, missing rollback action, excessive step limit, and undeclared sensitive data.
turns.expected_stems: return every violation stable sorted order first error tests valid manifest write|coding write validate agent manifest python declare owner purpose allowed classes capabilities

turns.text: Observability-first debugging: the platform dashboard reports 99.9 percent successful responses, but Customer Service has dozens of confirmed wrong-answer cases. Produce the investigation query plan, not a narrative. Show how you join request traces, tool results, publication decisions, escalation records, and downstream case outcomes; identify likely denominator or sampling bugs; and define the corrected reliability metric with its inclusion and exclusion rules.
turns.expected_stems: produce investigation query narrative request traces results publication decisions escalation records downstream|observability first debugging platform dashboard reports percent successful responses customer service dozens

turns.text: A senior stakeholder demands launch this week and calls your evaluation gate bureaucracy. Create the rollout contract you would put in front of them: non-negotiable safety conditions, negotiable scope reductions, canary population, owner, SLOs, outcome guardrails, stop conditions, and evidence review cadence. Then state exactly where you would concede and where you would escalate.
turns.expected_stems: create rollout contract would front negotiable safety conditions scope reductions canary population|senior stakeholder demands launch calls evaluation bureaucracy create rollout contract would front

turns.text: You inherit a distributed team that can operate Python services but has little agent-systems experience. Produce a thirty-day mentoring artifact with weekly deliverables, code labs, design reviews, office hours, paired incident drills, and ownership transfer. Define competency using inspectable code and operational evidence, not course completion or attendance.
turns.expected_stems: produce thirty mentoring artifact weekly deliverables design reviews office hours paired incident|inherit distributed operate python services little agent systems experience produce thirty mentoring

turns.text: Close the incident with a blameless but technically sharp postmortem. Give five action items in a table with owner, due date, failure mechanism, proposed control, and proof of effectiveness. At least two actions must change the system, one must change detection, one must change rollout policy, and none may be vague items such as improve communication or add more testing.
turns.expected_stems: action items table owner failure mechanism proposed control proof effectiveness least change|close incident blameless technically sharp postmortem action items table owner failure mechanism

interviews.focus: Adversarial defense of the candidate's claimed systems, with explicit concessions, falsifiable evidence, scalability analysis, and implementation proof

turns.text: Your receipt-gated Tau orchestration sounds like process tax wrapped in cryptographic language. Quantify it. Give me a table for latency, compute cost, storage, implementation complexity, operator friction, and failure-detection value with and without receipts. State the workload size at which receipts stop paying for themselves, and name one class of task where you would remove them entirely.
turns.expected_stems: table latency compute storage implementation complexity operator friction failure detection value without|receipt gated orchestration sounds process wrapped cryptographic language quantify

turns.text: An immutable goal hash proves only that you consistently pursued some text, not that the text was correct. Attack your own design. Give one bad-goal example, one goal-substitution attack, and one stale-evidence attack that all pass a naive hash check. Then specify the additional authority, freshness, dependency, and approval evidence needed before a receipt can support a production claim.
turns.expected_stems: example substitution attack stale evidence naive check specify additional authority freshness dependency|immutable proves consistently pursued correct attack design

turns.text: Live coding: using only the Python standard library, implement verify_run(goal_hash, planned_tasks, receipts). Each receipt has task_id, goal_hash, input_hash, output_hash, dependency_receipt_hashes, status, started_at, and completed_at. Detect missing or duplicate receipts, goal mismatch, unknown tasks, dependency-hash mismatch, execution before dependencies, failed required tasks, and impossible timestamps. Return a typed result containing all violations in deterministic order, then add three adversarial tests.
turns.expected_stems: detect missing duplicate receipts mismatch unknown tasks dependency execution before failed required|coding using python standard library implement verify planned tasks receipts input output

turns.text: You claim more than 340 eval-gated capability contracts. That could be disciplined engineering or a vanity count. Show me the evidence that distinguishes them. Define contract independence, meaningful failure coverage, external validity, mutation sensitivity, flaky-test policy, and retirement criteria. Then choose ten representative capabilities and explain how you would audit for self-serving fixtures and gates that merely assert the implementation's own output.
turns.expected_stems: define contract independence meaningful failure coverage external validity mutation sensitivity flaky policy|claim gated capability contracts could disciplined engineering vanity count

turns.text: Your realtime evidence copilot was proven on one workstation with one 24-gigabyte GPU. That is not a platform result. Redesign it for a multi-tenant AWS environment using EKS or an equally concrete deployment model. Produce the capacity model, state partitioning, autoscaling signals, GPU and CPU fallback policy, tenant isolation, backpressure, failure domains, and cost envelope. Explicitly identify which local-first properties you lose and whether that invalidates the product claim.
turns.expected_stems: produce capacity model state partitioning autoscaling signals fallback policy tenant isolation backpressure|realtime evidence copilot proven workstation gigabyte platform result

turns.text: Observability-first debugging: every CI evaluation passes, but production users report unsupported answers. Traces show retrieval.hit_count=0, no recorded fallback_reason, publication=true, and no empty-retrieval examples in the golden set. Walk me through the evidence chain before proposing a fix. Identify the production invariant that failed, the evaluation blind spot, the immediate containment, the trace assertion, and the mutation or agentic test that would demonstrate the new gate is not theater.
turns.expected_stems: through evidence chain before proposing identify production invariant failed evaluation blind immediate|observability first debugging every evaluation passes production users report unsupported answers traces

turns.text: You built ArangoDB-plus-vector retrieval and NIST or MITRE control-to-evidence mapping for defense work. Why should I believe that transfers to brokerage? Produce a four-column table: transferable mechanism, direct evidence, fintech-specific gap, and bounded pilot. Include authorization, temporal financial state, auditability, customer harm, tax or compliance interpretation, and data-retention differences. Concede at least two gaps that cannot be solved by renaming entities.
turns.expected_stems: include authorization temporal financial state auditability customer compliance interpretation retention differences concede|built arangodb vector retrieval mitre control evidence mapping defense should believe transfers

turns.text: You also cite Lean 4 compiler-in-the-loop verification. Write one theorem statement you could honestly prove about an agent workflow, list every trusted assumption outside the theorem, and give a counterexample showing how the running system can still fail while the theorem remains true. Then tell me whether formal proof is the highest-value control here or an expensive distraction.
turns.expected_stems: write theorem statement could honestly prove about agent workflow every trusted assumption|compiler verification write theorem statement could honestly prove about agent workflow every

turns.text: Final challenge: you have budget to productionize one claimed system and must stop investing in another. Produce a decision table using customer value, regulatory risk, evidence maturity, scalability, operating cost, reversibility, and time to falsification. Choose, defend, and state what evidence would make you reverse the choice. Finish with a thirty-day experiment whose result can genuinely disconfirm your preferred bet.
turns.expected_stems: choose defend state evidence would reverse choice finish thirty experiment whose result|final challenge budget productionize claimed system investing another decision table using customer

coverage_approval.verdict: sufficient - do not add a sixth interview
coverage_approval.thin_spot: Strands-native implementation fluency - prescribed as a 45-minute closed-book coding drill, not an interview
